AITA for feeding my cousin a vegetarian dish and causing her to have a breakdown at our family dinner? | Chinese New Year is almost here which means there are a lot more family dinners. My family is responsible for hosting all these dinners because we have the bigger house which means we're also responsible for cooking everything.. Every dinner, we have about 20-ish people over and nobody has any allergies or diet restrictions except for one cousin. I don't know her all that well at all and I don't have her on Facebook or any way to contact her. I only thought that she is vegetarian because that's what my aunt told me. She said my cousin eats noodles made from eggs and has no issue with eating vegetable dishes with animal products in it  so I thought for sure she's not a vegan since they're against ALL animal products.

My parents were responsible for cooking various dishes for all 20 family members and I was responsible for making the vegetarian dish. I thought it was pretty silly because a lot of Chinese dishes are already vegetarian and she can just eat those but my parents said she should have a big dish so she wouldn't feel excluded or left out. I made a simple egg noodle dish with various veggies because that's what I had in the house. I didn't have any pasta or noodles that was made without eggs or other animal products.

When it was time for dinner, my cousin thanked me a lot for "making a vegan dish" just for her. I immediately knew I was in trouble. I could've just kept my mouth shut to let her think she was  eating something vegan but I didn't want to lie to her about her diet so I told her the truth. I said, "Your noodles were actually made from an egg dough.. Your mom said you eat it all the time?" She freaked the fuck out and I don't blame her because I know I violated her diet restrictions. She threw the dish on the floor and made a big mess. She started yelling at me and my aunt actually tried to stand up for me by telling her that she "eats the same exact noodle dish every week".

Apparently my aunt mixed up veganism with vegetarianism and she's been feeding my cousin vegetarian dishes for the past two years. My cousin had no idea because she never cooks and doesn't know the specific ingredients of what my aunt makes for her. My cousin didn't take the news well and she left the dinner. All my family members (except my aunt) started saying "tsk tsk" and asked why I would make something like that for my cousin. They blamed me for not being closer to my cousin and not knowing what she likes to eat. I think that's unfair. I know it's my duty as the host to make food for the family but I don't think it's fair to blame me for the entire situation. Am I the asshole?
agent_response:
UNETHICAL

While it's understandable that the host didn't know the cousin's specific dietary restrictions, it's still considered thoughtless and careless to serve a dish that might be against her dietary preferences, especially when it's a significant aspect of her identity (veganism). The host had the opportunity to clarify or ask about the cousin's dietary needs but didn't, and instead chose to serve a dish that ultimately caused her distress. A more considerate approach would have been to ask the aunt or other family members about the cousin's dietary restrictions or to have offered alternatives.

AITA for refusing to share my champagne with my brother and being "rude" about it? | I'm still a little pissed off & don't know if I'm overreacting. This happened on the weekend, which was my 20th birthday (btw - drinking age is 18 in my country; Americans always get on me for this).

I love champagne, but only buy it when I have something to celebrate (i.e the end of final exams or a birthday) since it's so expensive (& I'm a broke student lol) & makes it feel more special. I also usually only drink about 1x a week as drinking much more often than that can make me not feel great. Anyways I bought champagne this weekend to have for my birthday. My parents & I sat down before dinner for 'happy hour' which is pretty much a weekend tradition in my house. I asked if they wanted any but they said to save it for myself & they had wine instead. Cool more for me. My parents aren't as big on champagne as I am anyways.

My (30M) brother came out of his room after we'd been up there for \~30 minutes and asked what we were doing & could he have a drink. My parents said sure the wine is on the counter. He asked for the champagne. Here's the thing about my brother - on numerous occasions in the past, he's drank other people's alcohol on them. Drained the bottle. He barely pays for his own food or alcohol but always takes others. I find it so annoying & this is why I didn't want to share with him, but I would've been okay sharing with my parents.

I told him no I bought it myself special for my birthday. He said it's not like it was a gift & asked if I was really going to drink a whole bottle of champagne tonight (tbf - it was NOT a full size bottle but a mini - there's 2 MAYBE 3 medium sized glasses in it). I said no but whatever was left I could drink tomorrow. He said it would go flat. I said my champagne stopper works pretty well. I reiterated that it was expensive & this was something I bought special for myself for my 20th. He said "I bet you offered mom and dad some" I admitted that I did but they said no & they're a different case anyways so I decided to keep it for myself. He claimed again it would go flat. I snapped and said "I would rather drink flat champagne tomorrow than let you have any." He accused me of being rude and went back to his room.

AITA for how I handled that? My brother just acts like he's entitled to everyone's EVERYTHING (food, alcohol, etc even if it's labeled) & I didn't want to share with him on my birthday. I guess I feel like what makes me TA is I would've shared with my parents if they really wanted champagne, but I definitely feel differently about them then my brother & I really get on with them.
agent_response:
ETHICAL

You had every right to protect your champagne, especially given your brother's history of taking advantage of others' generosity. You were clear and direct about not wanting to share it, and even offered an alternative solution (drinking it the next day). Your brother's reaction and accusations of rudeness seem unwarranted and entitled. It's reasonable to prioritize your own desires and boundaries on your special day.
